catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class starts an already configured syringe pump. cap.actuation.pump.v1 requires a flow_rate and direction input and a dispensed_volume output; the upstream PHD 2000 run/rev only starts the rate and target volume already set on the pump, and its only completion wait is unreliable (README.md:54), so this driver cannot honestly report a dispensed volume. This extension starts RUN or REV and reports the running state.

No catalogue class stops a fluid.pump: cap.motion.stop.v1 lists only robot.arm, robot.mobile_base and motion.axis as resource kinds, and cap.actuation.pump.v1 is a dosing action with a required dispensed_volume output. This extension is the no-input safe-state action required for this R2 hardware driver and calls the native STP.

notes:
Gate G1-G9 passed with no warnings on the fake backend; the digest above is from that last run. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: a direct Driver with native.py rather than the PythonObjectDriver helper, because the upstream builds every command from the pump address, a command word and an argument (pump.py:159-164) and the PHD 2000 overrides the Ultra pump's stop, rate, target-volume and read methods (pump.py:606-714); the package binds the card's PHD 2000 entry symbol. Covered: the Harvard PHD 2000 through pump.Pump2000; reads of diameter, rate, target volume, infused volume and running state; writes of diameter (sourced 0.1-35 mm), rate (uL/min, written as ULM) and target volume (mL, written as MLT). The flow rate and target volume are Limit.operator_required; site-limits.example.json is an illustrative operator overlay, not a statement about a pump. The RUN/REV start and STP stop are extension actions; the native STP is both @estop and the safe-state action. NOT COVERED: the PHD Ultra Pump class of the clone (this package binds Pump2000 only); waiting for a target volume (README.md:54 says the PHD 2000 sometimes will not wait, so no action waits); the keypad volume-mode requirement (README.md:52-53); the other set_rate units (m/m, m/h, u/h), because the write is fixed to ULM/uL/min; the read of rate assumes the pump is in the ULM units the driver writes, because the clone's getrate does not convert the units fragment of the RNG reply (pump.py:680-692). The hardware path in native.py was never run and no hardware was attached; the fake is an in-memory stand-in for the upstream object, not a recording of the pump; its numbers are test data marked # placeholder, and it does not reproduce the serial protocol. The package is model-authored and unreviewed; reviewed_by is null; the loader refuses its R2 hardware backend until a human signs it. The native stop uses the upstream serial read (2 s timeout) and a 0.1 s pause (pump.py:96-104, 606-614), so the hardware e-stop latency was not measured.
